newsitem.title: INDIA: India's NALCO to submit expansion plan.
newsitem.headline: India's NALCO to submit expansion plan.

text.p: India's state-run National Aluminium Company Ltd (NALCO) said on Wednesday it will submit a proposal to the government next month for the expansion of its aluminium smelter and captive power plant in the eastern state of Orissa.

"We are working on the cost of expansion proposal. The revised estimate will be submitted to the government next month for its approval," NALCO chairman S.N. Johri told Reuters in the Orissa capital Bhubaneshwar.
Last year NALCO officials had said they expected government approval of the expansion plan by December 1996. But the plan has not yet been submitted.
Johri said the expansion of its smelter plant at Anugul is expected to cost about 25 billion rupees.
NALCO plans to expand its annual smelter capacity to 350,000 tonnes from 230,000, tonnes and step up its power plant capacity to 960 megawatts from 760.
Officials had earlier said the project was expected to take around 50 months to complete from the date of approval.
Johri said the expansion work, expected to take around four years, would be funded by internal resources, external borrowings and the capital market.
In November India approved the expansion of NALCO's bauxite mines to 4.8 million tonnes per year from 2.4 million, and of its alumina refinery to 1.575 million tonnes from 800,000.
The expansion of the bauxite mines and alumina refinery will involve an investment of 16.65 billion rupees and take 51 months.
NALCO, Asia's largest aluiminium maker, produced 192,288 tonnes of aluminium in 1995/96 (April-March) against 178,072 tonnes in the previous year.
It has a domestic market share of 35 percent and state-of-the-art technology for alumina and aluminium production.
The company hopes to achieve a net profit of 5.1 billion rupees in 1996/97 against 5.4 billion in the previous year.
